metadata.method: supplier-balanced, Huber-robust additive log-price model with exact rational identification of month contrasts

model.equation: log price(s,m,i) = item_level(i) + month_effect(m) + supplier_level(s) + error
model.weights: each supplier trajectory has equal total weight; a quote gets 1/n_s for its supplier, rescaled to mean 1
model.error_assumption: var(error) = sigma^2 / base_weight; within-supplier correlation is not modelled parametrically but is preserved by trajectory resampling
model.outlier_handling: Huber IRLS, tuning 1.345 on MAD-standardized residuals; quotes are downweighted, never deleted, so all observed support stays in the design
model.product_semantics: families are used only to label old/new replacement pairs; they are not equivalence keys for estimation

design.note: Pivot columns are a maximal independent set of the design; they are used for fitting so no numerical routine decides rank.

uncertainty.method: whole-supplier-trajectory bootstrap with replacement; identification re-tested exactly in every replicate; percentile intervals
uncertainty.resampling_unit: supplier trajectory (all quotes of one supplier)
uncertainty.coverage_note: Percentile intervals from a finite supplier bootstrap are descriptive; no exact finite-sample coverage guarantee is claimed. Replicates that lose identification are failures, not zero estimates.

limitations: The model is additive on log prices with persistent item and supplier levels; if relative SKU prices drift within the six-month window the month effect is biased toward the average drift.
Families only record a replacement relationship. Any old/new level difference reported here is a measured persistent level difference from overlap, not a quality or equivalence claim.
Identification is exact and conditional on the observed quote pattern; absence of overlap is reported as insufficient support rather than bridged with external product prices.
Supplier-level disturbance dependence is handled only by whole-trajectory resampling; no parametric covariance model is fitted.
Percentile bootstrap intervals are descriptive and may be optimistic when the bridge rests on a single supplier, which is shown explicitly by the delete-one stability table.
No forecasting, hedonic regression, rolling analysis or automatic product matching is performed.
